headline: Ajax favourites at home — but by only a quarter of a goal
summary: Ajax lost 1-2 at Hajduk Split last Thursday, so this home tie with Atalanta already matters. Sunday brought a 5-2 win at Groningen, and Daley Blind and Steven Berghuis have rejoined the group, according to Voetbalzone. Atalanta arrive with their coach under public pressure: La Repubblica reports Sarri's position is on the line after 3 defeats in 5. Even so, the market makes Ajax only 44.7% favourites — rated about a quarter of a goal better, which is home advantage more than a gulf in class. The goal line is 3.0.
read: Ajax come home off a 5-2 win at Groningen but with a European defeat in Split already on their record, while Atalanta arrive with their coach reported to be under pressure after a 3-2 loss at Milan. The market makes Ajax 44.7% favourites but rates them only about a quarter of a goal better, and expects a game around the three-goal mark.

facts.fact: Ajax are 44.7% to win at home, against Atalanta's 30.1%, with the draw at 25.3%.
facts.meaning: Ajax are clear favourites in front of their own crowd, but Atalanta keep a live chance — this is not priced as a one-sided tie.

facts.fact: La Repubblica reports that Sarri's position at Atalanta is on the line after three defeats in five, with Thiago Motta and Tudor named as possible substitutes, though the club is said to retain confidence in him for now.
facts.meaning: Atalanta travel to Amsterdam with their coach under public scrutiny — every game now carries extra weight for them.

facts.fact: Ajax lost 1-2 at Hajduk Split last Thursday in the Conference League.
facts.meaning: Their only European result so far is a defeat, which is why a home match already feels important for Ajax.

facts.fact: Ajax won 5-2 at Groningen on Sunday.
facts.meaning: They arrive in Amsterdam scoring freely, which is the football reason the market makes them favourites here.

facts.fact: Atalanta lost 3-2 at AC Milan on Sunday, having been dominated for an hour before a late fightback.
facts.meaning: Their fightback shows they stay in games, but the first hour is exactly the pattern their coach has admitted to.

facts.fact: Daley Blind and Steven Berghuis rejoined Ajax's group training a day before the Atalanta match, according to Voetbalzone.
facts.meaning: Two experienced options back in the group right before kick-off is a boost for the home side.

facts.fact: Ajax are 25th of 36 in the Conference League table with 0 points from their opening game.
facts.meaning: A home match is already a chance to get off the mark in the league phase.

facts.fact: Atalanta sit 4th of 36 in the Conference League table after winning their opener.
facts.meaning: Despite the domestic noise around the coach, Atalanta arrive ahead of Ajax in the league phase.

sources.fact: Ajax beat FC Groningen 5-2 on Sunday and Míchel Sánchez is expected to make several changes for the Atalanta match, Voetbalzone reports.
Daley Blind and Steven Berghuis have rejoined Ajax's group training a day before the Atalanta match, according to Voetbalzone.
Ajax lost 2-1 to Hajduk Split last Thursday in the Conference League, a result Goal describes as humiliating.
Ajax coach Míchel Sánchez said at his post-match press conference that Jofre Torrents had not played badly against Hajduk Split despite the 2-1 defeat.
Ajax coach Míchel Sánchez and Marc ter Stegen will hold the pre-match press conference at the Johan Cruijff ArenA on Wednesday at 14:00.
Atalanta coach Maurizio Sarri said: "In every match we do well for 30–40 minutes, but we alternate good spells with moments of major limitations."
La Repubblica reports that Sarri's position is on the line and that Thiago Motta and Tudor are possible substitutes, with the club retaining confidence in him for now.
Atalanta lost 3-2 at AC Milan in Serie A on Sunday, having been dominated for an hour before mounting a fightback.
